name: Barbados
summary: Barbados has no forced heirship for children, but a surviving spouse can ask the court for a larger share of the estate. Barbados has a private foundation law. The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
family_claims: A surviving spouse can apply to the court for a share, or a larger share, of the estate on testacy, intestacy or partial intestacy (a Caribbean family-provision text names Barbados among the exceptions to unrestricted testamentary freedom). The statute was not identified.
foreign_law_note: No source read states Barbados's conflict rule for a foreign national's estate. Common-law rule: movables follow the law of the domicile, land follows local law. Not confirmed in local statute for this jurisdiction.
trust_note: Barbados is not in the HCCH status table. Common-law trusts apply; no Barbados trust statute was read. IFC Review lists Barbados among Caribbean states with private foundation laws (the Act's name was not confirmed).
open_questions: Family provision statute and any rights for children or dependants not identified.
Foundation Act name and terms not confirmed.
Barbados trust statutes and any firewall provision not read.
